strategy.summary: Pure-Python sympy bug in EllipticCurve.__add__ (P + (-P) vertical-line check). Reproduce by running the single test function test_elliptic_curve in sympy/ntheory/tests/test_elliptic_curve.py on the buggy commit 6fcc30bbfa6f and on its fixed successor. No compiled code, no numerical backend, exact integer arithmetic. Python version and curve-constructor signature are not stated in the evidence and must be read from the checkout. Main risk: the added test point (0,0) may not exercise the buggy branch at all.
strategy.test_command: cd sympy && bin/test sympy/ntheory/tests/test_elliptic_curve.py -k test_elliptic_curve (fallback: python -m pytest sympy/ntheory/tests/test_elliptic_curve.py::test_elliptic_curve)
strategy.reproducing_test: sympy/ntheory/tests/test_elliptic_curve.py::test_elliptic_curve, with the added lines: curv = EllipticCurve(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0); assert (curv(0,0,1) + -curv(0,0,1)).z == 0
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 6fcc30bbfa6f the test_elliptic_curve test fails at the new assertion, because (P + -P).z is not 0 (or the branch does not return the point at infinity). On the fixed revision, where the vertical-line check is (y1 + y2 + a1*x1 + a3) == 0, the same test passes with z == 0. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
risks: The test point (0,0,1) may satisfy y1+y2==0 as well (y1=y2=0), in which case the buggy code may already return infinity and the test would not fail on the buggy revision. Verify by running the test on the buggy commit before relying on the transition.

The constructor argument order and count (six arguments) must be checked against the checked-out EllipticCurve signature; a3 and a1 values determine whether the bug trigger (a1 or a3 nonzero) is met at all.
Verify that (0,0) lies on the curve for these parameters; if not, the test may raise an error on both revisions rather than transition.
The fix condition is inferred from the code diff and commit message only; no formula is stated in the passages beyond -P = (x, -y - a1*x - a3).
Behaviour is exact integer/rational arithmetic, so no platform, architecture, BLAS, or sanitizer dependence is expected; the defect is not expected to depend on architecture.
sympy version is unconstrained in the evidence (no documented or era ceiling), so the checkout commit determines the sympy version and no pip pin is applied.
Test runners listed in the evidence (./setup.py test, bin/doctest) are not needed; bin/test or pytest suffices for this test function.

oracle.why: Point at infinity is represented by z == 0 in projective coordinates; the check is exact integer equality.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion (curv(0,0,1) + -curv(0,0,1)).z == 0 is expected to see a nonzero z (or fail to reach infinity) on the buggy revision if the buggy vertical-line check misses the a1*x1 + a3 term for this point; this is not verified and depends on the point being on the curve and on the trigger holding.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the condition (y1 + y2 + a1*x1 + a3) == 0 and -P = (x, -y - a1*x - a3), the sum returns the point at infinity and z == 0, so the assertion holds.
